content.title: About
content.content: Pork is the meat of the domestic pig, rich in protein and B‑vitamins. Combined with carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (such as spinach or kale), the dish gains extra fiber, vitamins A, C, K and minerals like potassium and magnesium. Prepared without potatoes or tomato‑based sauce, it fits low‑carb dietary patterns.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its anti‑cancer properties.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables are excellent sources of folate and vitamin K.
When cooked properly, pork stays tender and juicy while the vegetables retain a crisp texture.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork provides complete animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: The meat supplies thiamine, niacin and vitamin B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Broccoli and carrots deliver antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber and minerals
items.content: Leafy greens add dietary fiber, potassium and magnesium, promoting healthy digestion and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Absence of potatoes and tomato sauce makes the dish suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: Very fatty cuts of pork can be hard to digest for people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Cooking temperature
items.content: Pork should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F) to eliminate salmonella and trichinella risks.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Some pre‑made seasonings may contain monosodium glutamate, which can trigger sensitivity in certain individuals.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should moderate intake of spinach and other high‑oxalate greens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the pork into thin strips and mixing with steamed or lightly sautéed vegetables. It works as a main course, a filling for wraps, or tossed into a fresh salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it remains good for up to 2 months after cooling to room temperature.
